Subject: Discovery follow-up: model-fit benchmarks & quantization trade study

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + coding suggestions (avg input ~1.2k tokens, 95th ~3.5k).
- Success metrics: token-level latency <75ms (p50), accuracy on clinical entity extraction >= 91% (existing internal eval), and deterministic safety filtering for PHI redaction.
- Constraint: data must stay in US region (we’ll use our us-central private cluster for the PoC).

Preliminary model recommendations (based on the prompt set you shared):
- Family A (7-13B instruction-tuned): best quality/latency balance for shorter summaries.
- Family B (30B dense) or quantized 34B variants: higher quality on complex records, higher cost/latency.

Quantization / throughput trade study we propose to run for PoC:
1) Baseline: FP16 dense run for Family A (7B) and Family B (30B) to get accuracy baseline and latency.
2) AWQ (adaptive weight quantization) on 7B/13B to test op-level throughput gains; expect ~1.8–2.5x token/sec improvement vs FP16 with minimal quality drift on summarization prompts, but we’ll validate across your entity extraction checks.
3) GPTQ (per-channel static quant) on 30B-class models to test cost-first path; expect larger quality delta — we’ll capture rouge/f1 drop and failure modes.
4) FP8 experimental path for 13B as an exploratory high-throughput option (only if accuracy holds on edge cases).

Deliverables we’ll share in 5 business days after we get your confirmation and the ground-truth eval set:
- QuickBench results: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and per-prompt accuracy for each quant/config option (script + CSV).
- Prompt set we’ll use (insightmed_promptset_v1.txt).
- One-page trade study summarizing AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 with clear recommended default for PoC.

Requests from your side (small asks so we can start):
- Confirm we can run the eval on the sample data (non-production PHI-masked set) in US region.
- Share the canonical gold labels or a short list of priority cases (10–30 examples) for the initial regression check.
- Any hard SLO requirements for tail latency or cost target (per 1k tokens).

Attachments: insightmed_promptset_v1.txt (prompt list), redwood-bench-quickrun.sh (bench script).

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min sync next week to kick off the bench and loop in Engineering (Marissa + Rishi) to run the first pass.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear notes, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a PHI-masked sample set (30 examples) this week — I’ll attach the file to the next message.
- Target constraints: we’d like p50 latency under 60ms if possible (we know it’s tight) and a cost target of <$0.04 per 1k tokens for inference to be viable at scale. If those are impossible we just want a clear migration path.
- Compliance: data residency must be US-only and audit logs retained for 90 days (we’ll need a simple evidence artifact for SOC-type checks).

We’re curious about expected quality drift numbers — do you have any prior internal numbers for AWQ on the 7–13B family when the task is summarization + extraction? Also would you include a short table in the output that flags whether any prompt produced hallucinations on the gold set?

If Marissa can join the bench run that’d be great. I’m okay with a kickoff next Tue/Wed morning (ET).

Appreciate the quick reply — yes to all asks. Short answers:
- We’ll aim for p50 < 60ms for the 7B-class pathway (AWQ optimized) and will surface tradeoffs if we can hit it only with higher memory configs.
- Cost modeling: we’ll include per-1k token cost estimates for each configuration (baseline FP16 / AWQ / GPTQ / FP8).
- AWQ historical: in our internal SummEval runs AWQ on 7B instruction-tuned variants resulted in median Rouge-L drop of ~0.5–1.2 points across summarization sets; extraction F1 typically within 1–2% of FP16 except in edge-case long-context probes. We’ll validate specifically on your entity list.

Plan: Marissa/Rishi will run two quick passes next week — 1) 7B family FP16 vs AWQ on the 30-sample gold set, 2) 30B-class GPTQ probe on a subset (5 examples) to measure worst-case regressions. Expect preliminary CSV + notes within 3 business days of the run.

I’ll schedule Tue 10/6 10:30am ET for a 30-min kickoff (invite coming) — confirm if that works and we’ll send a calendar invite and include a short test plan.

Aditya

1) Environment: us-central private cluster (sandbox network), bench image redwood/bench:202610, log retention 90d enabled.
2) Run 1 (full): 7B-family FP16 vs AWQ — script redwood-bench-quickrun.sh on insightmed_promptset_v1.txt (30 examples). Collect per-prompt latency, tokens/sec, Rouge-L, entity-F1, and hallucination-flag (boolean).
